Sb7m7FoRf10.title: Surah As-Saffat: Ilyas, Lut and Yunus (37:123-148)
Sb7m7FoRf10.one_line: Why As-Saffat tells the stories of Ilyas, Lut and Yunus briefly: each demands accepting the unseen and judgements whose wisdom is hidden.
Sb7m7FoRf10.summary: He restates the surah's axis: submission to Allah both in matters wholly unseen and in commands whose wisdom we cannot grasp, and shows how the stories of Nuh, Ibrahim and Musa fit it. Ilyas is a prophet the Arabs never knew and the Quran barely describes; the Torah's account may be heard but neither believed nor denied, so accepting him as Allah presents him is itself faith in the unseen. Along the way he explains the grammar of 'the best of creators', the difference between a messenger with a law and a prophet, and why 'seal of the prophets' closes both. Lut's story is told without the closing praise given to other prophets because his name has been dragged into the sin of his people. He argues that the prohibition stands whether or not its full wisdom is understood, then speaks frankly: desire is innate but its direction is shaped by upbringing, culture, abuse and other factors; the sin is the act, not the feeling; oversimplifying the issue has cost Muslims the argument. Disapproval never permits injustice toward anyone. Finally, Yunus's people were spared while Lut's were destroyed, and no one can claim to know why. He asks for submission, careful understanding and fairness.

outline.heading: Every surah has its own axis
outline.gist: Recap: the stories in a surah serve the purpose for which it was revealed, and each surah of this group looks at obedience differently.

outline.heading: Two kinds of hidden: unseen realities and unseen wisdom
outline.gist: Some things, like angels, are known only through revelation; some commands have reasons we cannot reach. As-Saffat addresses obedience in both.

outline.heading: Recap: Nuh's ship and Ibrahim's sacrifice
outline.gist: Both were commanded to do what made no visible sense and obeyed.

outline.heading: Why Musa's story is compressed here
outline.gist: Elsewhere each surah picks a distinctive part of Musa's story; here it is summarised because all of it fits the axis.

outline.heading: Musa's life as a chain of puzzling commands
outline.gist: Cast into the river, raised in Pharaoh's palace, sent to Madyan, called at the fire, sent to the sea, told to enter the gate: each time he obeyed without knowing the end.

outline.heading: Ilyas: a prophet we barely know, and the idol Baal
outline.gist: After reciting the passage he notes that Ilyas appears only here with a story; Baal was a Canaanite deity of strength, likely linked to Baalbek.

outline.heading: "The best of creators" and the grammar of substitution
outline.gist: The superlative glorifies Allah without implying rival creators; Allah, your Lord and Lord of your forefathers are appositives sharing the same case, with another reading parsing it differently.

outline.heading: The Torah's account of Ilyas and Al-Yasa'
outline.gist: A king married a Canaanite princess, idol worship spread, the queen threatened Ilyas, and in that account he was raised up and prophethood passed to Al-Yasa'.

outline.heading: Rejection, the sincere servants, and peace upon Il-Yasin
outline.gist: His people denied him and will be brought to account; the greeting is extended to his followers, and we accept the wording without knowing why.

outline.heading: How to treat reports from the People of the Book
outline.gist: They may be narrated but neither believed nor denied; anything contradicting the Quran is rejected, and prior law is used in rulings only when nothing else exists.

outline.heading: Messengers whose stories we were not told
outline.gist: The Prophet spoke at length about many prophets but said nothing about Ilyas; some messengers are simply unknown to us.

outline.heading: Mursal, rasul and nabi; the seal of the prophets
outline.gist: A rasul brings a new law, a nabi follows an earlier one; because Muhammad is the seal of the prophets, neither prophet nor messenger comes after him.

outline.heading: Which prophets followed earlier laws
outline.gist: Lut followed Ibrahim's law, Ilyas, Yunus, Zakariyya and Yahya followed Musa's, while Isa brought a law that lifted some prohibitions.

outline.heading: The purpose of Ilyas's story: accepting what we do not know
outline.gist: The surah names a prophet and gives almost no detail, teaching acceptance of the unseen as part of faith.

outline.heading: Lut: rescued with his family except an old woman
outline.gist: Recitation of the passage, noting that it ends differently from the other stories.

outline.heading: An indecency no one had committed before
outline.gist: Lut was sent to a people whose conduct went against sound nature, something a man in ordinary circumstances would find repugnant.

outline.heading: Forbidden even when the full reason is not clear
outline.gist: Harms of zina are obvious, the wisdom here may be harder to spell out, but what Allah forbids is forbidden; the pork-worm argument shows how weak invented reasons can be.

outline.heading: Different upbringing, same prohibition
outline.gist: People raised elsewhere relate to the issue differently, yet the ruling stays.

outline.heading: Why Lut is not given the lasting good mention
outline.gist: Unlike the other prophets, Lut is not followed by the line of praise among later generations, because his name is still attacked; with Allah he is among the greatest.

outline.heading: Punishments heaped on Sodom; a word derived from his name
outline.gist: The city was lifted, struck, stoned and overturned; scholars disliked naming the act after Lut, who had nothing to do with it.

outline.heading: Why his wife was destroyed
outline.gist: She did not commit the act, but approved of it; she is the Quran's example of a disbeliever married to a righteous man.

outline.heading: The wisdom is clearer in our age
outline.gist: With the practice now widespread we understand more of the prohibition than earlier jurists; declining civilisations show its spread alongside luxury and excess.

outline.heading: "You pass by them morning and night"
outline.gist: Quraysh's caravans passed the ruins of Sodom and were asked to reflect.

outline.heading: Be slow to judge those raised in the West
outline.gist: Arabs who grew up rejecting this instinctively should understand why others think differently, without accepting the act.

outline.heading: Desire is innate; its direction is shaped
outline.gist: Culture, home, schooling, personal experience and especially childhood abuse shape the direction of desire, just as food tolerance is shaped.

outline.heading: Examples from villages, prisons and ships
outline.gist: Men deprived of women for long periods commonly redirect desire, which fiqh books addressed in detail.

outline.heading: The sin is the act, not the feeling
outline.gist: He knew young men, including huffaz, with no attraction to women who still avoided sin; great scholars lived and died unmarried.

outline.heading: Oversimplifying lost the argument
outline.gist: Claiming no one is born otherwise was easy to refute; classical fiqh was more aware than Muslims today, and children imitate what they see.

outline.heading: Direction can be guided; orientation is not identity
outline.gist: Teaching sexual choices to seven-year-olds confuses them; attraction in youth is common and not a label, and what matters is conduct.

outline.heading: Lut's patience over losing his good name
outline.gist: He bore being deprived of praise among people; avoid using the term derived from his name.

outline.heading: What the wife actually did
outline.gist: Answering a question: she informed the people about his guests, a form of approval rather than participation.

outline.heading: Rejecting a sin never permits injustice
outline.gist: Hatred of a people's deeds must not lead to unfairness; fight ideas with ideas and laws with laws, but never accept that anyone be wronged.

outline.heading: Yunus: the laden ship and the whale
outline.gist: Recitation of the passage, noting that Yunus too lacks the closing praise.

outline.heading: Yunus leaves Nineveh in anger; the lots and the whale
outline.gist: Sent to what is now Mosul, he left angry at his people once punishment was decreed; the lots fell on him three times and he was swallowed, blameworthy.

outline.heading: Why Yunus's people were spared and Lut's were not
outline.gist: The outcomes differ completely and no one can claim to know the reason; we accept Allah's decree.

outline.heading: Outro

28:22.en: And when he turned his face toward Midian, he said: Peradventure my Lord will guide me in the right road

28:23.ar: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيۡهِ أُمَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسۡقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمۡرَأَتَيۡنِ تَذُودَانِۖ قَالَ مَا خَطۡبُكُمَاۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسۡقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصۡدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيۡخࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
28:23.en: And when he came unto the water of Midian he found there a whole tribe of men, watering. And he found apart from them two women keeping back (their flocks). He said: What aileth you? The two said: We cannot give (our flocks) to drink till the shepherds return from the water; and our father is a very old man

28:24.ar: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَآ أَنزَلۡتَ إِلَيَّ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَقِيرࣱ‏
28:24.en: So he watered (their flock) for them. Then he turned aside into the shade, and said: My Lord! I am needy of whatever good Thou sendest down for me

28:25.ar: فَجَآءَتۡهُ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا تَمۡشِي عَلَى ٱسۡتِحۡيَآءࣲ قَالَتۡ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدۡعُوكَ لِيَجۡزِيَكَ أَجۡرَ مَا سَقَيۡتَ لَنَاۚ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفۡۖ نَجَوۡتَ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:25.en: Then there came unto him one of the two women, walking shyly. She said: Lo! my father biddeth thee, that he may reward thee with a payment for that thou didst water (the flock) for us. Then, when he came unto him and told him the (whole) story, he said: Fear not! Thou hast escaped from the wrongdoing folk

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

33:32.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ لَسۡتُنَّ كَأَحَدࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيۡتُنَّۚ فَلَا تَخۡضَعۡنَ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَيَطۡمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ مَرَضࣱ وَقُلۡنَ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
33:32.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Ye are not like any other women. If ye keep your duty (to Allah), then be not soft of speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to you), but utter customary speech

c8UBSTNBN4M.title: Contemporary Issues: Principles of Gender Relationships
c8UBSTNBN4M.one_line: From Musa at Madyan, he sets seven categories of male-female relationships and five problems that arise when a relationship has no defined premise.
c8UBSTNBN4M.summary: He reads the story of Musa at the well of Madyan to reject both extremes: that men and women can never interact safely, and that there are no limits. Musa approached two women to help, they answered, and one returned with haya, which he explains as ethical sensitivity rather than giggling shyness. He then lists seven categories: unmarriageable relatives, other relatives, knowledge-based, professional, social acquaintance, necessity, and spouse. Interaction is acceptable when it has a clear premise and stays within its parameters, as the Prophet's open masjid and a physician's conduct show. Five problems follow from undefined relationships: calling someone simply a friend, flirting, which belongs with your spouse, forbidden private settings, including one-on-one texting, staring rather than shying away the gaze, and forbidden mixing, though he prefers an open masjid where people learn respect over full segregation. In the second part he stresses that Islam values clarity, so interest in marriage should be stated openly and courtship differs from dating, that zina is among the gravest sins and its paths begin with the eyes, that chastity is behaviour as well as dress, and that young people's need for intimacy deserves open discussion.

outline.heading: Opening
Musa reaches the water of Madyan
outline.gist: Cross-gender relations are central to the ethical code at any age. Musa arrives where people gather at the water and sees two women holding back their flock, a verb used only for animals.

outline.heading: He speaks to the women and they answer
outline.gist: Musa does not ignore them as none of his business: a stranger, he starts the conversation; they explain their elderly, pious father, he waters their flock and leaves.

outline.heading: Haya as ethical sensitivity
outline.gist: The woman who returns walking with istihya is not giggling or embarrassed; she comes professionally and respectfully to deliver her father's invitation.

outline.heading: The story rejects both extremes
outline.gist: Neither 'men and women can never interact safely' nor 'no limits': the Quran has many examples of non-mahram interaction accepted within parameters.

outline.heading: Category one: maharim
outline.gist: Those you can never marry: very open, you can travel and be alone with them; if there is fear of attraction the relationship moves to another category.

outline.heading: Category two: other blood relatives
outline.gist: Relatives you could technically marry, such as a father's cousin, have different limits from the maharim.

outline.heading: Category three: knowledge-based
outline.gist: A man teaching a woman or learning from her, or the reverse.

outline.heading: Category four: professional
outline.gist: Colleagues and classmates brought together by shared work or study.

outline.heading: Category five: social acquaintance
outline.gist: For example a friend's wife you know socially.

outline.heading: Category six: necessity
outline.gist: Physician and patient, or saving someone who is choking; this was Musa's situation at the well.

outline.heading: Category seven: spouse
outline.gist: The seventh and final category.

outline.heading: The missing premise is the problem, not the relationship
outline.gist: Maharim are easy and the spouse is where sexual expression belongs; everything between needs a defined premise. An-Nur 24:30-31: believers lower their gaze and guard their chastity.

outline.heading: The Prophet's open masjid had clear parameters
outline.gist: One open space, men in front and women behind, where people knew what interaction was lawful and how to respect each other's movement; he wants this back.

outline.heading: Teacher, colleague, neighbour: talk within the premise
outline.gist: He was taught by women scholars and teaches girls; with colleagues and neighbours the nature of the relationship limits what is discussed.

outline.heading: The physician: set parameters make odd acts acceptable
outline.gist: A doctor can do things that look strange from afar because expectations are clear, and loses his licence or worse if he goes beyond them; even outside religion people accept this.

outline.heading: Problem one: the undefined word 'friend'
outline.gist: Friendliness is fine, but 'friend' alone allows anything and leaves expectations unclear; attach a category to it so the relationship is safe.

outline.heading: Problem two: flirting
outline.gist: The Quran's term for soft, suggestive speech: hinting instead of being clear, exciting because it is ambiguous. Every problem he has seen, married or not, began this way.

outline.heading: Flirt with your spouse; be friendly without flirting
outline.gist: Flirt with your wife or husband all day; couples stop after marriage and send it elsewhere. Smile and be kind, but step back when that tone appears, since outside the seven categories there is nothing.

outline.heading: Problem three: forbidden settings behind closed doors
outline.gist: Full seclusion with no one knowing is where most regretted mistakes began; medicine itself uses chaperones.

outline.heading: Virtual seclusion: one-on-one texting
outline.gist: A private chat no one sees and that can be deleted is where Shaytan has a heyday and most problems he sees start; professional texting is fine, but text within groups.

outline.heading: Problem four: the sinful gaze
outline.gist: Looking at someone you speak to is respectful; staring is not, so shy away when you notice it. If you cannot shake the habit, do not pass it to your children.

outline.heading: A conditional verse: true believers look away
outline.gist: He reads 24:30 as conditional: if they are truly believers they will lower their gaze; if not, they keep staring.

outline.heading: Problem five: forbidden mixing
outline.gist: Ikhtilat became an Islamic term only in later centuries; he accepts it, since some kinds of mixing are genuinely wrong, though not all interaction is.

outline.heading: Segregation avoids the problem; an open masjid fixes it
outline.gist: The Prophet did not build two masjids; full segregation works for a while but leaves ethics unfixed. Open space is harder but teaches ethical sensitivity, the representative ethic of Islam, with teaching and forgiveness for mistakes.

outline.heading: Interlude
Point one: clarity and transparency; courtship not dating
outline.gist: If you think someone suits you for marriage, say so; Shaytan lives in ambiguity. Dating is undefined, while courtship, meeting in public and talking about life plans, is clear.

outline.heading: Point two: the gravity of zina
outline.gist: Most scholars rank it worse than murder; looking and talking are steps on its path, eyes and ears commit their own zina, and stopping short is Allah rescuing you. It ruins families and societies.

outline.heading: Point three: chastity is mentality and behaviour
outline.gist: Not only dress but how you look, think and speak; appearance matters for both, more so for women, with greater reward.

outline.heading: Point four: ethical sensitivity and the Prophet's door for women
outline.gist: Respect people's space; the Prophet gave women a door and had men wait so they could leave first without being jostled.

outline.heading: Young people deserve to talk about intimacy
outline.gist: Everyone has a right to intimacy and there is nothing shameful in saying so; families and communities should discuss it openly instead of hoping nothing happens.

outline.heading: Outro

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Such of you as put away your wives (by saying they are as their mothers) - They are not their mothers; none are their mothers except those who gave them birth - they indeed utter an ill word and a lie. And lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

58:3.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:3.en: Those who put away their wives (by saying they are as their mothers) and afterward would go back on that which they have said, (the penalty) in that case (is) the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. Unto this ye are exhorted; and Allah is Informed of what ye do

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who findeth not (the wherewithal), let him fast for two successive months before they touch one another; and for him who is unable to do so (the penance is) the feeding of sixty needy ones. This, that ye may put trust in Allah and His messenger. Such are the limits (imposed by Allah); and for disbelievers is a painful doom

49:2.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَرۡفَعُوٓاْ أَصۡوَٰتَكُمۡ فَوۡقَ صَوۡتِ ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَلَا تَجۡهَرُواْ لَهُۥ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ كَجَهۡرِ بَعۡضِكُمۡ لِبَعۡضٍ أَن تَحۡبَطَ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَشۡعُرُونَ
49:2.en: O ye who believe! Lift not up your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor shout when speaking to him as ye shout one to another, lest your works be rendered vain while ye perceive not

8:5.ar: كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَيۡتِكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لَكَٰرِهُونَ
8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:6.ar: يُجَٰدِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَقِّ بَعۡدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
8:6.en: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible

m_ACHpjrSKM.title: Sunday Tafseer: Surat Al-Mujadilah, Part 1 (Verses 1-4)
m_ACHpjrSKM.one_line: Khawlah bint Tha'labah argues with the Prophet over zihar, Allah affirms her, and the ruling and heavy expiation for zihar follow.
m_ACHpjrSKM.summary: He opens the 28th juz, fully Madinan and focused on organizing society, after recapping the Qaf to Hadid cluster as a series of life choices. Mujadilah begins with Khawlah bint Tha'labah, an early Ansari Muslim whose elderly husband pronounced zihar on her, declaring her like his mother: she was neither divorced nor truly married, and could not object without insulting his mother. The Prophet had no revelation, so she argued with him. He stresses that Allah's statement that He heard her is not literal hearing, which is a given, but affirmation and approval of her argument, and that the surah is named after the woman who argued. The point is the society the Prophet built, where a woman felt safe to challenge him over injustice; Umar later stood listening to her rebuke. He then explains the ruling: wives are not mothers, and no one can change kinship status by a statement. Zihar was known to be wrong even in Jahiliyyah, which leads into the Muslim role of strengthening a society's good values and reforming its bad ones, with body-image pressure on young women as a modern example. He covers false speech as a major sin, the expiation of freeing a slave, fasting two months or feeding sixty, and how Khawlah paid it herself.

outline.gist: Both Mujadalah and Mujadilah are authentic names for the surah.

outline.heading: Khawlah bint Tha'labah: an early Muslim of Madinah
outline.gist: She accepted Islam in the first year after the pledge with the Ansar, outlived the Prophet by about fifteen years, and was married to Aws, brother of Ubadah ibn as-Samit; he invites listeners to find the surah's thread themselves.

outline.heading: What zihar was: a trick to punish wives
outline.gist: Saying you are to me as my mother left a wife neither married nor divorced, often for years.

outline.heading: Why she could not object socially
outline.gist: Objecting meant implying she was better than his mother, a question no wife could answer safely.

outline.heading: She brings it to the Prophet: no revelation yet
outline.gist: After a long, happy marriage her husband said it in anger; the Prophet told her he had nothing on it.

outline.heading: The Prophet's limits: rulings must come from revelation
outline.gist: She asked for a ruling, not an opinion, and he would not speak on law from intuition; she argued that it could not be permitted.

outline.heading: Would we accept a woman arguing like this today?
outline.gist: He suspects such a woman would be shunned in our communities, yet Allah recorded her argument positively and named the surah after it.

outline.heading: Two meanings of Allah has heard
outline.gist: Literal hearing is a given; the verse means figurative hearing: understanding and acknowledging her.

outline.heading: Allah affirmed her argument
outline.gist: She was right to stand her ground; some scholars say the Prophet could have offered an opinion, a view he does not hold.

outline.heading: She felt comfortable to argue: what the verse documents
outline.gist: Raised by the Quran and the Prophet, she knew it was her place to speak when something was unjust; Allah chose to give this ruling with a story.

outline.heading: A society designed for people to speak safely
outline.gist: Not an invitation to yell at imams, but proof that the Prophet built a community where people could raise problems.

outline.heading: Khawlah rebukes Umar as caliph
outline.gist: Years later she stopped Umar to advise him at length; he said the one Allah heard above seven heavens deserves to be heard by Umar.

outline.heading: Contrast: do not raise your voices above the Prophet
outline.gist: Abu Bakr and Umar were warned for loud arguing and afterwards whispered near him, yet Khawlah's argument was praised.

outline.heading: Contrast: arguing before Badr was blamed
outline.gist: Companions who argued against going out were chastised; argument over injustice is different.

outline.heading: An ummah where people feel safe to speak
outline.gist: We have not built that openness, for women or others; the surah reminds us it should exist.

outline.heading: Her legacy as a teacher of women
outline.gist: She lived long after and taught the women of Islam.

outline.heading: Recitation note: the many madd in these verses
outline.gist: He walks the audience through two-, four- and five-count elongations in verse two.

outline.heading: Their wives are not their mothers
outline.gist: Saying it does not make it true.

outline.heading: No one can change kinship status by a statement
outline.gist: Mahram status comes from birth and its extension through nursing, not from a man's claim.

outline.heading: Munkar as a social term, not only a religious one
outline.gist: Ma'ruf and munkar refer to what a community recognizes as good and bad, which Islam takes seriously.

outline.heading: Strengthen society's good values, reform its bad ones
outline.gist: Muslims support shared values like opposing drug abuse or kindness, and call for reform where society's values diverge from Islam's.

outline.heading: They knew zihar was wrong and let it continue
outline.gist: The verse says they knew; alcohol and cannabis are a modern case of known harm tolerated in moderation.

outline.heading: Can Muslims in the West be reformers?
outline.gist: He admits he does not know how, since we cannot yet keep our own youth from doubting or teach them Arabic; Jahiliyyah needed radical change because wrongs were left too long.

outline.heading: A modern known wrong: beauty standards imposed on young women
outline.gist: Telling girls their worth depends on height, weight or figure is toxic and serves those who profit from it.

outline.heading: His daughter, oversexualization and endless images
outline.gist: Islam's dress rules protect dignity, but today's flood of photos and graphic standards are ruining minds; we should speak like Khawlah did.

outline.heading: The effect on marriages and families
outline.gist: Delayed, smaller and less stable families are part of the harm we stay silent about.

outline.heading: Zur: false speech among the gravest sins
outline.gist: The Prophet repeated his warning against false testimony so intensely the companions wished he would stop; a lie can ruin a generation.

outline.heading: Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving
outline.gist: After a heavy verse Allah opens the door: repent and do right and you will be forgiven.

outline.heading: Recitation note: the six-count madd
outline.gist: A madd followed by a doubled letter is always six counts in the Hafs reading used here; other regions use other readings.

outline.heading: Expiation: freeing a slave before touching
outline.gist: One who wants to retract must free a person before resuming relations; Allah is aware of what is inward.

outline.heading: Otherwise two consecutive months of fasting, or feeding sixty
outline.gist: The expiation steps down only if the previous one is impossible.

outline.heading: Expiation as proof of belief; punishment for refusing
outline.gist: Allah never accepts this oppression; kafirin here means those who refuse to expiate.

outline.heading: Khawlah pays the expiation herself
outline.gist: Her husband could do none of the three, so the Prophet contributed dates and she covered the rest to keep her marriage.

outline.heading: Expiation in practice today
outline.gist: The verses are applied to similar oaths; people feed sixty, roughly a thousand dollars.

outline.heading: The weight of the expiation shows the weight of the sin
outline.gist: It matches the expiation for breaking a Ramadan fast by intercourse, far heavier than most; one verse of affirmation, three of ruling.

outline.heading: Outro

58:5.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَآدُّونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ كُبِتُواْ كَمَا كُبِتَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ وَقَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَآ ءَايَٰتِۭ بَيِّنَٰتࣲۚ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابࣱ مُّهِينࣱ‏
58:5.en: Lo! those who oppose Allah and His messenger will be abased even as those before them were abased; and We have sent down clear tokens, and for disbelievers is a shameful doom

58:6.ar: يَوۡمَ يَبۡعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَيُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُوٓاْۚ أَحۡصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
58:6.en: On the day when Allah will raise them all together and inform them of what they did. Allah hath kept account of it while they forgot it. And Allah is Witness over all things

58:7.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجۡوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمۡ وَلَا خَمۡسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ذَٰلِكَ وَلَآ أَكۡثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كَانُواْۖ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا عَمِلُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
58:7.en: Hast thou not seen that Allah knoweth all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth? There is no secret conference of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, nor of less than that or more but He is with them wheresoever they may be; and afterward, on the Day of Resurrection, He will inform them of what they did. Lo! Allah is Knower of all things

58:8.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نُهُواْ عَنِ ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُواْ عَنۡهُ وَيَتَنَٰجَوۡنَ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِۖ وَإِذَا جَآءُوكَ حَيَّوۡكَ بِمَا لَمۡ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ ٱللَّهُ وَيَقُولُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَوۡلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا ٱللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُۚ حَسۡبُهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُ يَصۡلَوۡنَهَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
58:8.en: Hast thou not observed those who were forbidden conspiracy and afterward returned to that which they had been forbidden, and (now) conspire together for crime and wrongdoing and disobedience toward the messenger? And when they come unto thee they greet thee with a greeting wherewith Allah greeteth thee not, and say within themselves: Why should Allah punish us for what we say? Hell will suffice them; they will feel the heat thereof - a hapless journey's end

58:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا تَنَٰجَيۡتُمۡ فَلَا تَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡعُدۡوَٰنِ وَمَعۡصِيَتِ ٱلرَّسُولِ وَتَنَٰجَوۡاْ بِٱلۡبِرِّ وَٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِيٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
58:9.en: O ye who believe! When ye conspire together, conspire not together for crime and wrongdoing and disobedience toward the messenger, but conspire together for righteousness and piety, and keep your duty toward Allah, unto whom ye will be gathered

58:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ لِيَحۡزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَلَيۡسَ بِضَآرِّهِمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
58:10.en: Lo! Conspiracy is only of the devil, that he may vex those who believe; but he can harm them not at all unless by Allah's leave. In Allah let believers put their trust

58:1.ar: قَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّتِي تُجَٰدِلُكَ فِي زَوۡجِهَا وَتَشۡتَكِيٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسۡمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ
58:1.en: Allah hath heard the saying of her that disputeth with thee (Muhammad) concerning her husband, and complaineth unto Allah. And Allah heareth your colloquy. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

58:2.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَآئِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِهِمۡۖ إِنۡ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡ إِلَّا ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي وَلَدۡنَهُمۡۚ وَإِنَّهُمۡ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنكَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡقَوۡلِ وَزُورࣰ اۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورࣱ‏
58:2.en: Such of you as put away your wives (by saying they are as their mothers) - They are not their mothers; none are their mothers except those who gave them birth - they indeed utter an ill word and a lie. And lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

58:3.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُظَٰهِرُونَ مِن نِّسَآئِهِمۡ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةࣲ مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
58:3.en: Those who put away their wives (by saying they are as their mothers) and afterward would go back on that which they have said, (the penalty) in that case (is) the freeing of a slave before they touch one another. Unto this ye are exhorted; and Allah is Informed of what ye do

58:4.ar: فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ شَهۡرَيۡنِ مُتَتَابِعَيۡنِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَتَمَآسَّاۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَسۡتَطِعۡ فَإِطۡعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسۡكِينࣰ اۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۗ وَلِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
58:4.en: And he who findeth not (the wherewithal), let him fast for two successive months before they touch one another; and for him who is unable to do so (the penance is) the feeding of sixty needy ones. This, that ye may put trust in Allah and His messenger. Such are the limits (imposed by Allah); and for disbelievers is a painful doom

85:9.ar: ٱلَّذِي لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
85:9.en: Him unto Whom belongeth the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is of all things the Witness

MjUXFc7VKV8.title: Sunday Tafseer: Surat Al-Mujadilah, Part 2 (Verses 5-10)
MjUXFc7VKV8.one_line: Allah records every forgotten harm, is present in every secret meeting, and condemns the breakaway counsel that wrecks a community's collective decisions.
MjUXFc7VKV8.summary: He places Mujadilah in a Madinan cluster about organizing relationships in Muslim society, then takes a tangent urging everyone to sit with a qualified teacher to correct their recitation and to learn how the qira'at work. Verse five warns that those who defy Allah's rulings will be subdued; he links this to Arab resistance to the new rules and to the Prophet's consultative leadership, using the Khandaq negotiation with Ghatafan and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's refusal. Verse six says Allah counted everything while people forgot it, which he calls the summary of Judgment Day: small, careless harms to others are recorded. Heavy Quranic language attaches to harming people because, once you cross that line, Allah forgives His share but you must repair the rest with the person. He adds the comfort that unseen sacrifice, including parents' care, is never lost. Verse seven teaches that a god who is not all-knowing is no god, and that Allah's presence in secret meetings is by knowledge, not physical. His main argument is that najwa means breakaway lobbying that undermines a group's agreed decisions, which he sees as the reason Muslim institutions fail. If private counsel happens, it must aim at excellence and taqwa; concerns should be raised openly.

outline.heading: The series and the Madinan cluster of Mujadilah to Tahrim
outline.gist: Unlike the preceding Makkan groups, this cluster is late Madinan.

outline.heading: Cluster theme: organizing relationships in Muslim society
outline.gist: Mujadilah organizes relationships among Muslim peers, beginning with ending the oppression of zihar.

outline.heading: Recap: Khawlah's dispute and Allah's affirmation
outline.gist: Dispute is a better rendering; she was commended and Allah's hearing means acknowledgement.

outline.heading: Organization, not manners
outline.gist: Other surahs teach ethics; this one sets parameters for what is and is not acceptable.

outline.heading: Recitation note: the six-count madd
outline.gist: A madd followed by a doubled letter is always six counts in the common Hafs reading.

outline.heading: Learn how the qira'at work
outline.gist: Understanding the readings protects you from being unsettled later by an unfamiliar recitation.

outline.heading: An imam in Damascus and speaking to people's level
outline.gist: A visiting reciter's unfamiliar reading caused panic; an imam must give people what they can receive, as one would not teach chemotherapy regimens to first-year students.

outline.heading: Sit with a teacher and accept correction
outline.gist: Every teacher he recited to told him everything was wrong; take a tajweed course at least once and learn by accepting feedback.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those who defy Allah and His Messenger will be subdued
outline.gist: Kubitu carries meanings of silencing, removal and punishment, as with nations before.

outline.heading: Ayat as clear signs
outline.gist: Most often ayat in the Quran means signs of truth, not verses.

outline.heading: Arab resistance to the new rulings and to consultation
outline.gist: Losing control over wives felt like ripping off a bandage, and tribal chiefs mocked the Prophet for asking people's opinions.

outline.heading: Khandaq: negotiating with Ghatafan
outline.gist: The Prophet offered a mercenary chief part of Madinah's dates to withdraw, then insisted on consulting the owners of that wealth.

outline.heading: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh's answer
outline.gist: Once he confirmed it was not a divine command, he refused; leaders need people behind them with grit in hard moments.

outline.heading: The heavy expiation that upset them
outline.gist: Sixty days of fasting or feeding sixty people, about a thousand dollars today.

outline.heading: Allah counted it all and they forgot it
outline.gist: He calls this the summary of Judgment Day, worth hanging over your bed.

outline.heading: Why this follows zihar: no oppression is small
outline.gist: Allah takes every act of transgression seriously, however minor.

outline.heading: The careless word that drops a person into Hell
outline.gist: A comment, smirk or post you never thought about can be what condemns you.

outline.heading: Facing forgotten harms on Judgment Day
outline.gist: You will not recognize the people you hurt, but it mattered to them and it is recorded.

outline.heading: Heavy wording attaches to harming others
outline.gist: Where the sin is between you and Allah, the Quran inserts tawbah; where it is oppression, the language is far more daunting.

outline.heading: Crossing the red line of human harm
outline.gist: Much of his counselling is people asking how to undo harm to others, and he honestly does not know.

outline.heading: Allah forgives His share; you must repair the rest
outline.gist: Allah wants to forgive, people do not; you must fix the harm with the person yourself.

outline.heading: Harms that cannot be undone, and gossip
outline.gist: Returned money cannot return lost years; for gossip you must go back to the same people, correct it and pray for the one you wronged.

outline.heading: The comfort: nothing you gave is lost
outline.gist: Your suffering and unappreciated service are recorded even if people forget.

outline.heading: Every moment of your parents' care is recorded
outline.gist: Years of care cannot be repaid; how will you answer for how you treated them?

outline.heading: Shahid: witnessing as it happens
outline.gist: A rare name in the Quran: Allah is present in the moment, not reviewing later.

outline.heading: Interlude
A god who is not all-knowing is not God
outline.gist: Belief in God entails omniscience; without it worship is pointless.

outline.heading: Ignorance is weakness
outline.gist: Our anxieties come from not knowing what is next; Allah has no such weakness.

outline.heading: No secret meeting of three without Allah as the fourth
outline.gist: The phrasing means presence with them, not a count.

outline.heading: Presence by knowledge, not physical presence
outline.gist: Physical means contained by space, which cannot apply to Allah; the verse opens and closes with knowledge.

outline.heading: What you say in private will be recited back to you
outline.gist: The verse prepares for the next ruling on najwa.

outline.heading: Interlude
Najwa is more than two people excluding a third
outline.gist: That etiquette matters, but he reads the verse, with classical commentators such as al-Zamakhshari, as about something larger.

outline.heading: Breakaway counsel that undoes collective decisions
outline.gist: After a group decides, small groups meet secretly and break what was agreed, in sin, aggression and disobedience.

outline.heading: Why does Allah not punish us?
outline.gist: Not being punished now is no proof of being right; Hell is sufficient for them.

outline.heading: How side groups wreck boards and committees
outline.gist: To ruin anything, join a board and start a side group; it destroys open, proper process.

outline.heading: They had already been told: and it is never positive
outline.gist: The verse implies an earlier prohibition; breakaway talk is always about what someone said or did wrong.

outline.heading: The traditional reading: a corrupted greeting
outline.gist: Some greeted the Prophet with a wish of death instead of peace; he accepts this but reads the verse thematically too.

outline.heading: Why Muslim institutions fail
outline.gist: The meetings after the meeting build a different narrative and sink the ship.

5nDwVZ7a5yE.title: Surah As-Saffat: Yunus, Tasbih and the Pagan Claims About Angels (37:139-160)
5nDwVZ7a5yE.one_line: Yunus's tasbih in the whale teaches how to meet what we cannot understand: glorify Allah, blame yourself, and stop chasing the unseen.
5nDwVZ7a5yE.summary: He opens with the difference between the seen world, which science keeps expanding, and the unseen, which even ancient and atheist philosophers acknowledged. Prophets alone link the two, so attempts to photograph jinn or diagnose possession are futile, and chasing unseen details breeds doubt and even shirk. Turning to Yunus, he explains that the prophet left Nineveh angry at his people, not at Allah, and that leaving without permission broke a rule binding on prophets, which is why the Quran calls him a runaway. Ibn Abbas's answer to Mu'awiyah clarifies that Yunus thought Allah would not constrain him, not that He lacked power. The key lesson is that Yunus was saved for being among those who glorify: tasbih means refusing to attribute any flaw to Allah when something painful or incomprehensible happens, as Isa answers on Judgment Day and as every bowing in prayer trains. The real calamity is only one that takes your faith. In the closing passage, the pagan Arabs' tale that angels are Allah's daughters by the jinn shows how speculation about the unseen grows step by step into a false religion, just as modern exorcism culture did. He asks believers to glorify Allah and leave what He has hidden.

outline.heading: Opening
The surah's axis and a God beyond the senses
outline.gist: As-Saffat concerns obeying Allah in the unseen and where wisdom is hidden; Allah perceives all but is not perceived.

outline.heading: Science expanded the seen world
outline.gist: We moved from a sun that circles us to galaxies measured in light-years, and modern people concluded the unseen is just the not-yet-discovered.

outline.heading: Philosophers always distinguished the unseen
outline.gist: From the Greeks onward, and even among atheist philosophers, the existence of an unmeasurable unseen was accepted; they disputed only how religions handle it.

outline.heading: Photographing jinn and angels is absurd
outline.gist: What could be photographed would belong to the seen world by definition.

outline.heading: Prophets as the only link; claims of possession
outline.gist: Prophets carry revelation from the unseen to the seen; describing jinn possession like a diagnosable illness is a claim about the unseen with no evidence.

outline.heading: Chasing the unseen leads to doubt and shirk
outline.gist: Some things are made beyond our grasp, like equations some can never follow; we should seek the knowledge we are obliged to learn instead.

outline.heading: Recap: the stories of the surah
outline.gist: Ibrahim's sacrifice is central and tied to Hajj; each story shows a side of faith in the unseen.

outline.heading: Recap: Lut and why he lacks the closing praise
outline.gist: Lut was sent to a people not his own, and his name was later attached to their sin, so the line of praise is not given.

outline.heading: Yunus sent to Nineveh, a people not his own
outline.gist: Nineveh, today's Mosul, among the oldest cities; Yunus, from the descendants of Ishaq, was sent to strangers, for reasons we do not know.

outline.heading: He left angry at his people, not at Allah
outline.gist: Told their punishment would come in three days, he left angry at their choice.

outline.heading: Mu'awiyah, Ibn Abbas and "he thought We would not constrain him"
outline.gist: Ibn Abbas explained that the word is from restriction, not power, citing Al-Fajr.

outline.heading: Prophets may not leave without permission: the runaway
outline.gist: As the Prophet waited for permission before the Hijrah, Yunus should not have left; the Quran uses the word for a runaway slave.

outline.heading: The laden ship, the lots and the blameworthy prophet
outline.gist: To lighten the ship they drew lots three times and each fell on Yunus, who recognised Allah's decree and was swallowed while blameworthy.

outline.heading: Surviving inside a whale
outline.gist: Not impossible given the size of whales, yet the event remains unseen to us.

outline.heading: Saved by tasbih, not istighfar: what tasbih means
outline.gist: Tasbih is refusing to attribute any flaw or shortcoming to Allah when something hard happens; Yunus blamed himself, not his Lord.

outline.heading: Isa's answer on the Day of Judgment: "Glory be to You"
outline.gist: Asked whether he told people to worship him, Isa, who spent his life teaching tawhid, does not question Allah's decree but glorifies Him.

outline.heading: Bowing in prayer trains us to glorify
outline.gist: Ruku is for magnifying the Lord, so that when hardship strikes the self does not accuse Allah; He is not questioned about what He does.

outline.heading: Yunus's dua and the only real calamity
outline.gist: No Muslim calls with it in distress except that Allah relieves him, at least in the heart; a calamity is minor unless it takes your faith or values.

outline.heading: Tasbih in infertility, chronic illness and trials
outline.gist: Glorifying Allah is surrender to His wisdom when we cannot see it; he calls this possibly the most important point of the series in an age that thinks it has decoded everything.

outline.heading: Cast on the bare shore under a gourd plant
outline.gist: Weakened by the whale, he was sheltered by broad leaves that repel insects, then sent back to a hundred thousand or more who believed.

outline.heading: His slip recorded openly; "do not say I am better than Yunus"
outline.gist: Everyone errs, and the Prophet forbade claiming superiority over Yunus; why his people were spared is hidden from us.

outline.heading: Why these stories were chosen for As-Saffat
outline.gist: Elsewhere the Quran explains causes; here it picked the stories with the most mystery: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus.

outline.heading: Accept a command once it is established
outline.gist: Verifying that something is Allah's command needs knowledge and evidence; once clear, accept it without accusation.

outline.heading: Interlude
"Ask them": daughters for Allah and sons for them
outline.gist: Recitation of the closing passage; Allah challenges them to explain their claim.

outline.heading: The crime of burying daughters
outline.gist: The Quran condemns their shame at a daughter's birth and burying girls alive.

outline.heading: The myth: angels as daughters of Allah by the jinn
outline.gist: He mentions it once only because it is so offensive: they claimed Allah married from the jinn and the angels were His daughters.

outline.heading: How speculation about the unseen grows: exorcism sessions
outline.gist: Small claims pile up into a whole system; as a teenage hafiz he was taken to sessions full of fraud built the same way.

outline.heading: "Were they witnesses?"
outline.gist: Elsewhere people ask the Prophet for rulings; here they are asked, since they claim to know; like the count of the sleepers of the cave, it is unseen and pointless.

outline.heading: Inventing claims about Allah
outline.gist: Saying about Allah what He did not say is the end of chasing the unseen; one small lie builds into a tower of lies.

outline.heading: "Bring your book" and glory be to Allah
outline.gist: They have no proof; the passage ends with tasbih again, the surah's answer to what we do not understand.

outline.heading: Outro

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

24:33.ar: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ اۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنࣰ ا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:33.en: And let those who cannot find a match keep chaste till Allah give them independence by His grace. And such of your slaves as seek a writing (of emancipation), write it for them if ye are aware of aught of good in them, and bestow upon them of the wealth of Allah which He hath bestowed upon you. Force not your slave-girls to whoredom that ye may seek enjoyment of the life of the world, if they would preserve their chastity. And if one force them, then (unto them), after their compulsion, lo! Allah will be Forgiving, Merciful

2:235.ar: وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا عَرَّضۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ خِطۡبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوۡ أَكۡنَنتُمۡ فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡۚ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ سَتَذۡكُرُونَهُنَّ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تُوَاعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا إِلَّآ أَن تَقُولُواْ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ وَلَا تَعۡزِمُواْ عُقۡدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ فَٱحۡذَرُوهُۚ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
2:235.en: There is no sin for you in that which ye proclaim or hide in your minds concerning your troth with women. Allah knoweth that ye will remember them. But plight not your troth with women except by uttering a recognised form of words. And do not consummate the marriage until (the term) prescribed is run. Know that Allah knoweth what is in your minds, so beware of Him; and know that Allah is Forgiving, Clement

apamidcis18.title: Contemporary Issues: Principles of Gender Relationships (Part 2): The Rule of 5Ps
apamidcis18.one_line: Interactions between men and women not pursuing marriage rest on chastity and five rules: professional, pious, protective, parting and personable.
apamidcis18.summary: Building on last week's seven categories of cross-gender relationships, he explains that when marriage is not being pursued, whether because someone is married, too young, without means or uninterested, relationships rest on iffah, chastity, a neglected Islamic principle. Even marriage-related private talk must be something you could say publicly without shame. Two prophetic stories show his teaching style: the Prophet withheld his hand from a youth who had tugged a girl's garment the night before, and at the Farewell Hajj he gently turned his young cousin's face away from a woman asking a question. He warns young people that everything on social media is permanent, and parents that children starved of attention at home seek it online. His five Ps follow. Be professional and stay on the task, and admit that a nineteen-year-old is not really seeking marriage. Be pious by bringing a wandering gaze back. Have a protective mentality, which is what male leadership and the mahram rule mean, not control. Part where mixing brings no benefit, without full segregation. Stay personable and kind. Following these would save community projects, and secret relationships are a sign of going through the wrong door.

outline.heading: Opening
Iffah governs relationships when marriage is not the aim
outline.gist: The seven categories need attention, and the An-Nur verses set the conduct; if you are not pursuing marriage, the relationship rests on iffah, chastity, a central principle that has fallen out of discussion.

outline.heading: What 'not pursuing marriage' covers
outline.gist: Already married, too young, without means, a match that could never work, or the other side not interested: then live chastely until Allah grants a way (24:33).

outline.heading: Even marriage talk must be publicly sayable
outline.gist: Private talk with marriage in mind must still be honourable speech you would not be embarrassed to have shared (2:235); only within marriage do these limits lift.

outline.heading: The youth who tugged a girl's garment
outline.gist: A teenager in a visiting delegation wandered Madinah at night and tugged a girl's trailing garment; next morning the Prophet withheld his hand at the pledge, a public shock, until the boy promised never to do it again.

outline.heading: Al-Fadl at the Farewell Hajj
outline.gist: As a young woman questioned the Prophet, his cousin riding behind him stared, and the Prophet gently turned his face away; asked why, he said he did not feel safe from Shaytan for a young man and woman. No yelling, just a gesture.

outline.heading: The rule of five Ps is for everyone
outline.gist: He used to teach it to high school students, but people in their forties and fifties who ignore it also end up harming themselves or others.

outline.heading: Everything you put out is permanent
outline.gist: Every text, picture and post can be retrieved; it is unfair for a teenage mistake to haunt a whole life, and most such mistakes involve cross-gender relationships. Parents: children deprived of attention at home seek it online, so know what is on their phones.

outline.heading: Interlude
P1: professionalism
outline.gist: Stay within the seven categories and the task at hand, whether with an employer, employee, colleague or classmate.

outline.heading: A nineteen-year-old is not seeking marriage
outline.gist: His grandparents married at 13 and 14 in another context; today a high schooler is not ready, so stay focused, and once ready go through parents while remaining professional.

outline.heading: P2: piety
outline.gist: Eyes and mind will wander; taqwa brings them back. Show the taqwa you would want shown to your sister, mother, wife or daughter, since Muslims refuse double standards.

outline.heading: P3: a protective mentality
outline.gist: Islam flips the male predatory instinct: when dealing with the opposite gender you make sure they are safe and comfortable, even if they are the ones making a mistake.

outline.heading: Leadership and the mahram rule mean protection, not control
outline.gist: Control is self-serving and pleasant; protection demands sacrifice and self-control, including protecting her reputation from your own mistakes.

outline.heading: P4: parting
outline.gist: Separate when mixing brings no benefit, such as segregated prayer lines in one masjid; he rejects fully segregated masjids and schools, having grown up in them.

outline.heading: P5: personable
outline.gist: None of this means frowning and rudeness; a Muslim is kind, friendly and compassionate while keeping the other rules.

outline.heading: The five Ps would save community projects
outline.gist: Many projects in the community died because a problem between men and women was hushed up instead of these rules being followed.

outline.heading: Until you can marry, keep these rules
outline.gist: Young people's wish for intimacy is legitimate and he will help them pursue it; until then, apply the five Ps in every team and class.

outline.heading: The rookie move: a hidden relationship
outline.gist: The most common problem he hears is an attachment formed before parents agree; relationships should be celebrated, so if it must be hidden it is not the right one. Knock on the door.

outline.heading: Outro
